subject: french

items.q: Do all French verbs follow one pattern?
items.correct: No — there are regular (-er, -ir, -re) and many irregular verbs.
items.misconception: Yes, every verb conjugates the same way.
items.why: Common irregulars (être, avoir, aller) must be learned.

items.q: Does the perfect tense always use 'avoir'?
items.correct: No — some verbs and all reflexives use 'être' (and agree).
items.why: A set of verbs of movement/state, plus reflexives, take 'être'.

items.correct: Yes — they agree with gender and number (petit/petite/petits/petites).
items.why: Adjectives agree with the noun they describe.

items.q: Where do most French adjectives go?
items.correct: Usually after the noun (une voiture rouge).
items.misconception: Always before the noun, as in English.
items.why: A few common adjectives go before, but most follow the noun.
